subject: Finaxion vendor comparison — post-demo notes, decision criteria & next tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Grant <ag@finaxion.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Finaxion vendor comparison — post-demo notes, decision criteria & next tests

Hi Alicia — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on inference during batch payroll runs (peak windows) — currently hitting 800–1,200ms on your POC.
- Cost unpredictability: several models are used across teams with varying throughput and token patterns.
- Auditability: compliance team needs per-request audit logs + retention policy for 2 years.

Goals you want to hit in an evaluation
1) Stable 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for typical interactive flows (conservative SLO).
2) Predictable monthly inference cost within a 20% band of projections.
3) Clear audit logs and SOC2-aligned evidence for procurement.

How Redwood mapped to those today (summary)
- Serving runtime: continuous batching + KV caching can reduce token cost on repeat prompts; we observed potential 30–40% token reduction in similar customers.
- Routing/variants: can route payroll traffic to a higher-throughput pinned pool during nightly loads to avoid latency spikes.
- Compliance: Private deployment option + KMS integration meets audit/retention needs; we can provide SOC2 artifacts and sample retention configs.

Competitive bake-off snapshot (from today's demo and your notes)
- Redwood: strong routing/rollout controls, native auditing, and clear batching knobs. Potential gap: we will need to validate throughput at your peak sequence lengths.
- Vendor X (on your shortlist): lower latency in microbenchmarks but lacks request-level audit logs and limited rollout controls.
- Vendor Y: good cost for embeddings-heavy workloads; unclear on private deployment timeline.

Open technical questions we agreed to validate
- Can we reproduce Finaxion's payroll peak with a synthetic replay (sequence distribution attached)? [ACTION: Finaxion to share representative sequence histogram]
- Will Redwood Dedicated meet 95th pct latency at 1.2M tokens/hour for the payroll job? [ACTION: Redwood to run staged replay on Dedicated test pool]
- Exact retention policy format for audit logs (fields + export mechanism) — Alicia to confirm compliance fields.

Proposed next tests (timing)
1) Synthetic replay run — Redwood infra team to run replay on a Dedicated test slice (target week of 6/21). Deliverable: per-model latency distribution and failure modes.
2) Cost projection exercise — we'll run your sample month through our cost model and return line-item projections within 3 business days after the replay.
3) Compliance package + SOC2 excerpts — we’ll drop these into the shared Drive by EOD 6/11.

Attachments: finaxion-replay-histogram.csv (please confirm this is representative). Also attached a compact mutual action plan (finaxion-mutual-action-plan.xlsx).

Alicia — if that matches your view, can you confirm the replay data share and whether Procurement wants an NDA-first lane or is OK with the MSA-driven POC?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Finaxion vendor comparison — post-demo notes, decision criteria & next tests

Thanks Camila — very thorough, appreciate the clear steps. A few quick clarifications: 

- We will share the replay CSV (anonymized) by EOD Friday 6/11.
- Procurement prefers MSA-first for POCs (we have an internal checklist) — I copied Procurement.
- Compliance fields: we need request_id, model_version, timestamp, request_path, and hashed_payload in the audit log. I’ll attach a sample schema once I run it by the team.

One more ask: can Redwood provide a side-by-side one-pager that compares expected SLA behaviors (failover, routing, autoscale) versus Vendor X and Vendor Y? Procurement finds that format easiest to review.

Happy to run the replay early next week if that helps.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Platform Engineering, Finaxion
ag@finaxion.com

- Deliverable: CSV of latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), token throughput, and any errors (OOMs/timeouts). Will also include guidance on batching/kv-cache settings.
